# Document the recharge model (GDD + code comments)

## Goal

Bring the Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections, power-up levelling section, HUD presentation) and the relevant code comments up to date with the recharge model, so the written design matches the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections and the power-up levelling section) and relevant code comments are updated to describe the recharge model; the CHANGELOG is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded.
- The teleport and phase-shift sections of the Game Design Document describe recharging charge pools (per-charge timers, cap of 3, level-derived recharge time) and no longer claim unlimited activations for the permanent Phase Shift reward.
- The GDD power-up levelling section (§4.4) and HUD presentation describe the new recharge-time axes and the greyed-out-row behaviour for zero-charge pools.
- Relevant code comments in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` and `src/powerups/effects.ts` (module headers, consume/collect/resolver docs) match the recharge model.

## Minimal Implementation

- Edit `docs/Game Design Document.md` (teleport/phase-shift sections, power-up levelling + HUD presentation) and the two module header/comment blocks.
- The three out-of-scope follow-ups (recharge countdown bar, recharge-complete audio cue, gym recharge sliders) are already recorded as sibling work items.

## Dependencies

- HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows (behaviour finalised) and the recharge engine (model finalised).

## Key Files

- docs/Game Design Document.md
- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts
- src/powerups/effects.ts

# Verify full suite and typecheck pass with recharge changes

- `npm run typecheck` passes with no type errors.
- The game↔gym parity sweep (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`) is green.

## Dependencies

## Key Files

discovered-from:AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9

## Problem

Manual review of AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 (Bot steering model to consume live ShipConfig thruster values) reported: "When I click Watch Demo (or run a capture) the AI bot behaves totally differently to when I am watching it in the gym scene. The gym scene is correct."

Investigation verified the model layer is shared and identical between the demo and the tuning gym:
- Both scenes build the brain via createCompetentBotBrain({ tunables: toCompetentOverrides(getCurrentBotTuningConfig().values) }) (PlayScene._applyBotTuning / GymBotTuning._applyTuning).
- Both scenes build the snapshot via buildBotSnapshot carrying the live Player.getThrusterConfig(); diagnostic confirmed byte-identical thruster configs in both.
- The demo seam responds to a custom ShipConfig end-to-end (new tests in src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts).

The remaining 'totally different' behaviour is scenario-driven, not model-driven:
- The shipped demo (PlayScene) plays the live campaign: random offscreen asteroids (asteroidSpawnerEnabled=true), timed waves (getWaveState active → enemyWavePressurePort), lane traffic, harvesters, ghosts, boss encounters.
- The bot-tuning gym (GymBotTuning via generateRandomLevel) generates enemy-formation-only levels: the sequencer candidate pool filters out asteroid/harvester/grunt; there is no asteroid spawner, no timed waves and no boss.

## Goal

Make the bot-tuning gym exercise the same scenario pressures the shipped demo does — asteroids (with drift), timed waves, and optionally boss — so tuning in the gym transfers to the demo, and the demo does not behave 'totally differently' from the gym purely because of scenario content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. GymBotTuning (or the GymLevel base) can spawn drifting asteroids the same way PlayScene does (or reuse the shared spawn-planning helper), so the bot's hazard/asteroid responses are exercised.
2. The gym scenarios include timed waves (or an equivalent wave-pressure signal) so enemyWavePressurePort decisions are covered.
3. Demo↔gym observation: with the same bot tuning, the demo bot and gym bot make the same decisions given equivalent snapshots (no further divergence beyond scenario randomness).
4. Full test suite passes; gym↔game parity guard (CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts) remains green.

## Out of scope
- Any further change to the bot's decision model (already delivered by AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9).
- Changing the shipped game's demo scenario.
data.title: Bot-tuning gym scenario lacks asteroids/timed waves the demo plays (parity gap)

data.comment:
Rework after producer manual review ('Watch Demo behaves totally differently from the gym; the gym is correct').

Investigation findings (this session):
- The model layer is shared and identical between the demo and the tuning gym: both scenes build the brain via createCompetentBotBrain({ tunables: toCompetentOverrides(getCurrentBotTuningConfig().values) }) and the snapshot via buildBotSnapshot carrying the live Player.getThrusterConfig(). A diagnostic boot of both scenes with the same seed confirmed byte-identical thruster configs (300/175/100/true/200/120) and identical tunables mapping.
- The demo path consumes the live config end-to-end: setting a custom ShipConfig via Player.setConfig changes the demo's snapshot and flips the pure forward-model mayThrust decision (verified in the new tests).

Changes delivered inline:
- src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts: new 'Demo live-thruster config (AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9)' block pinning (a) the demo snapshot carries the live thruster config end-to-end (AC1), (b) a custom live config changes the demo's decisions with live values winning (AC2/AC5), (c) demo and tuning-gym apply the identical tunable mapping, explicit override > live > default (AC4).

Out-of-scope finding (recorded): the residual 'totally different' behaviour is scenario-driven — the shipped demo plays the live campaign (random asteroids, timed waves, lane traffic, boss) while the tuning gym generates enemy-formation-only levels with no asteroids/timed waves. This is tracked as AH-0MV9AWR7A0084XJ0 (discovered-from:AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9).
